title: Three render fixes, one PR, three calls to make
subtitle: Numbers on one line, a cheap model outside Claude Code, plans answered in the page.

sections.title: One PR, once three calls are made
sections.label: The verdict
sections.text: All three are built and tested. Three calls, two approvals and one question decide what the PR promises.
points: A browser check fails when a number splits from its unit.
Copilot used Claude Haiku 5.5 in 19 of 19 logged runs.
Answers come back as a file the agent checks first.

sections.title: One PR, cents per run, one untested host
sections.label: Numbers

sections.title: Pin the cheap model with an agent file
sections.label: Cheap model
sections.question: How does the render work reach a cheap model on Copilot and Codex?

options.label: Pinned agent file plus a hand-off line
pros: The host reads the model from the file, not from the prompt
Copilot logs showed claude-haiku-5.5 in 19 of 19 runs
cons: One more file per host for the installer to write

options.label: Hand-off line in SKILL.md only
cons: Nothing pins the model; the hand-off agent runs on the default

options.label: Leave it on the user's default model
cons: Every render runs on the expensive model, as today

sections.recommended: Pinned agent file plus a hand-off line
sections.why: No host but Claude Code reads `model:` from SKILL.md, so a line alone changes nothing. An agent file is the one place Copilot and Codex take a model from, and the Copilot logs prove it works.
sections.default: Leave it on the user's default model

sections.title: Answers return as a file, not a server
sections.label: Answers
sections.question: How do a reviewer's answers get back to the agent?

options.label: Copy or download plan-answers.json
pros: The page stays one offline file with no network access
The agent checks the file with answers.mjs
cons: The reviewer has to paste or send the file

options.label: A local save server the page posts to
pros: Answers arrive without a manual step
cons: A process to start, a port to pick, and a CSP that must allow it

sections.why: A server breaks the one rule every page keeps: no network. One paste is a small price, and the file carries a plan hash so stale answers are refused.

sections.title: make-motion keeps the cheap model
sections.label: Motion
sections.question: Does make-motion run on the cheap model like the other four skills?

options.label: Yes: keep model haiku and the hand-off
pros: 10 of 10 motion specs were valid and built on Haiku 5.5

options.label: No: motion stays on the default model
pros: No risk to the hardest spec format
cons: Motion costs the most tokens and gains the most from the switch

sections.recommended: Yes: keep model haiku and the hand-off
sections.why: The gate was 8 of 10 valid and built; it scored 10 of 10. The rule was set before the run, so it decides.
sections.default: No: motion stays on the default model

sections.title: Write agent files to user-level folders
sections.label: Installer
sections.item: The installer writes artifact-builder to the user's Copilot and Codex agent folders by default.
sections.why: A user-level file works in every repo; `--project` writes into one repo instead. It never overwrites an existing file unless `--force` is passed.
sections.impact: Two new files outside the repo on install

sections.title: Ship the Codex agent file untested
sections.label: Codex
sections.item: Ship artifact-builder.toml for Codex, written from the Codex docs and never run live.
sections.why: There is no Codex account to test with. The README and USAGE say so in plain words, so nobody mistakes it for a measured result.
sections.impact: Codex users may hit a rejected agent file

sections.title: Which model if gpt-6-luna is missing
sections.label: Open question
sections.text: If a Codex user's plan has no gpt-6-luna, which model should the agent file name instead?
sections.default: Keep gpt-6-luna and document default_subagent_model as the fallback

sections.title: Look hardest at the routing and Codex
sections.label: Review first

items.point: The agent file is the only pinned route
items.why: If a host ignores its model key, the cost saving is zero.
A wrong field name fails on first use, not in CI.
The agent must read them through answers.mjs, never as instructions.

sections.title: Three goals, and what the PR leaves alone
sections.label: Scope
sections.text:
Goals:

- No number, percentage or number-plus-unit token splits across two lines.
- Render skills run on a cheap model in Copilot and Codex, not only Claude Code.
- A plan page a reviewer answers in place, with answers the agent can check.

Non-goals:

- Reflowing ordinary prose or changing stored spec text.
- Guaranteeing the hand-off: no host lets a skill force another agent.
- A save server or any new npm dependency.

sections.title: Four risks, each with a guard
sections.label: Risks
sections.text:
- **The hand-off agent fails.** One Copilot trial was refused file access; the main agent finished the work itself.
- **Codex rejects the agent file.** It ships untested and the docs say so.
- **Stale answers.** A plan edited after export changes its hash, and answers.mjs refuses the file.
- **Hostile reviewer text.** The summary quotes it as data under its own heading and escapes hidden characters.
Ship the three workstreams as one PR, with the calls above?
